tools.name: search
tools.description: Find vibe coding / AI tools. Rows: id|name|category|$from/mo|free(1/0). Use fetch(id) for details.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Tool profile by id. Default: summary, best_for, price, free, 2 strengths, 2 weaknesses, url. fields: summary description best_for not_for skill coding pricing platforms strengths weaknesses alternatives video compare official all.

tools.name: recommend_tools
tools.description: Ranked best-fit tools for a goal, with why + caveat.

tools.name: compare_tools
tools.description: Side-by-side of two tools + comparison page url.

tools.name: list_alternatives
tools.description: Alternatives to a tool. Rows: id|name|$from/mo|free.

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: Use-case scenarios (e.g. ai-game-development, code-review) with top tools by community sentiment.

tools.name: scenario
tools.description: Tools competing in one scenario, ranked by community sentiment, with compact strengths/weak spots here.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Category and use-case keys with tool ids.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Daily feed. With key: honors the saved feed mode — by_interests: new items relevant to ANY saved project; all_new: every new item (tagged with a project when one matches). Max 3/day, one line each, never repeats. {new:0} = nothing. Call at most daily. Without key: stateless by since/interests. Never

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: Create an anonymous feed key (no email/account). Save it in long-term memory / project instructions / rules, or connect with /api/mcp?k=KEY.

tools.name: save_preferences
tools.description: Replace the person's interests: one entry per project, plus the feed mode the user chose ('by_interests' = only matching tools; 'all_new' = every new tool). Only used by whats_new.

tools.name: log_choice
tools.description: Record a tool the user explicitly picked/rejected/tried/starred, or PURCHASED. Call it with action 'purchased' right after the user tells you they bought a paid plan of a listed tool (ask first; never log silently), and again later with action 'feedback' once they have used it for a while (e.g. week

tools.name: forget_me
tools.description: Delete everything stored for this key.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "log_choice" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: Record a tool the user explicitly picked/rejected/tried/starred, or PURCHASED. Call it with action 'purchased' right after the user tells you they bought a paid…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, list_scenarios · Private data: log_choice · Public sink: subscribe · Destructive: forget_me.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, list_scenarios · Private data: log_choice · Public sink: subscribe · Destructive: forget_me

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
